title: People
goal: Describe what people are like and what they look like, point someone out ('the one who…'), talk about friends, partners and in-laws, and share (or stop) a bit of gossip.
intro:
Half of all conversation is about other people: the new flatmate, a friend's boyfriend, the sister-in-law who doesn't get on with anyone. In this unit you'll learn the words for what someone is **like** (funny, shy, stuck-up, hard-working) and what they **look** like, the family words Indians actually use (भाभी, जीजा जी, सास), and the English that's normal for modern relationships.

The grammar is about describing: full **relative clauses** — *the guy **who** wears glasses, the girl **whose** engagement it is, the friend **I** live **with*** — and the verbs **लगना** and **दिखना** for 'seems' and 'looks'. You'll also learn the little trap that turns 'she seems nice' into 'I fancy her'.

In relaxed talk about people, this unit uses **वो** *vo*, the spoken form of both वह and वे.

grammar.title: Relative clauses in full: जो, जिसका, जिसने, जिसके साथ…
grammar.body:
Unit 20 introduced the Hindi way of saying 'the one who…': a **j-word** in one clause and a matching **v-word** in the other. **जो** लड़का चश्मा पहनता है, **वो** मेरा भाई है 'The boy who wears glasses is my brother' (lit. 'which boy wears glasses, he is my brother').

To describe people precisely you need all the forms of **जो**. They work exactly like the forms of वो (उस, उसका, उसने, उसे):

**जो** — who / which (subject): **जो** लड़की लाल कुर्ते में है…
**जिस** + postposition — **जिससे** 'from/with whom', **जिसके साथ** 'with whom', **जिस** दुकान में 'in which shop'
**जिसका / जिसकी / जिसके** — whose: **जिसकी** सगाई है 'the one whose engagement it is'
**जिसने** — who (with ने, past of transitive verbs): **जिसने** यह कहा 'whoever said this'
**जिसे / जिसको** — whom, to whom
Plural: **जिन** (+ postposition), **जिनका**, **जिन्होंने**, **जिन्हें**

The j-word also goes **before a noun**, like 'which': **जिस** लड़के से मैं मिली… 'the boy I met…'.

**Order:** most often the j-clause comes first and the main clause starts with **वो**. You can also put it after the noun, English-style, between commas: वो दोस्त, **जिसके साथ** मैं रहता हूँ, बहुत आलसी है. Or at the end: मेरा एक रिश्तेदार है **जो** पुलिस में है.

**Shortcut with वाला:** for a quick label Hindi often skips the clause: **चश्मे वाला** लड़का 'the boy with the glasses', **लाल कुर्ते वाली** 'the one in the red kurta', **ऊपर वाले** 'the people upstairs'.

**The traps:** don't use कौन or क्या for 'who/which' inside a sentence (they only ask questions), and remember that जो changes before a postposition: never जो से, always **जिससे**.

grammar.title: Seems and looks: लगना, दिखना, जैसा, -सा
grammar.body:
**लगना** 'to seem' describes the impression someone makes. The adjective agrees with the person:

वो थका हुआ **लग रहा है** — he looks tired (right now)
वो बहुत अच्छी **लगती है** — she seems really nice (in general)
तुम आज स्मार्ट **लग रहे हो** — you look sharp today

**The big trap:** add **मुझे** and the meaning changes to *liking*: **मुझे** वो अच्छी लगती है = **I like her** (often: I fancy her). Without मुझे it's just an opinion; with it, it's a feeling. So तुम्हें वो अच्छा लगता है ना? is a friend teasing you about a crush.

**दिखना** 'to look, appear' is about **appearance**. **दिखने में** means 'looks-wise': **दिखने में** स्मार्ट है, पर बहुत घमंडी है 'he's good-looking, but really stuck-up'.

**Looks like someone:** X **जैसा / जैसी / जैसे** दिखना or लगना, with जैसा agreeing with the person described: वो अपनी माँ **जैसी** दिखती है, तुम अपने पापा **जैसे** लगते हो.

**लगता है (कि)…** at the start of a sentence means 'it seems / looks like': **लगता है** उनका झगड़ा हुआ है 'looks like they've had a fight'.

**-सा** after an adjective means '-ish, a bit': **अजीब-सा** 'weirdish', **पागल-सा** 'a bit crazy'. It agrees like an -आ adjective: अजीब-**सा** लड़का, अजीब-**सी** लड़की, अजीब-**से** लोग.

lines.speaker: Aditi

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: हा हा! और उसका भाई? उसकी तो किसी से नहीं बनती।

lines.speaker: Aditi

lines.native: अरे, शर्मा क्यों रही हो? बताओ ना!
lines.roman: are, sharmā kyoṃ rahī ho? batāo nā!

culture: Indian families have a word for every relative, and people use those words instead of names: your brother's wife is **भाभी**, your sister's husband **जीजा जी**, an older cousin is **भैया** or **दीदी**; a friend's wife is often called भाभी too. Elders are spoken about with the respectful plural even when they aren't there (उसकी मम्मी बहुत सख़्त **हैं**). Comments on looks are much more direct than in English: an aunty may tell you **तुम मोटे हो गए हो** 'you've put on weight' as a sign of affection, not an insult. Comments on skin colour (**गोरा** 'fair', **साँवला** 'dusky') are still common in older talk and matrimonial ads, but many young people find them offensive, so leave them out. **रिश्ता** covers both a relationship and a marriage proposal; you'll hear **लव मैरिज** and **अरेंज्ड मैरिज** in Hindi just like that. And gossip is a national sport, especially at weddings: if you don't want to join in, **छोड़ो, हमें क्या!** gets you out politely.

lessons.title: Saying what someone is like

tip.title: Describing someone
tip.body:
- Adjectives in **-आ** agree: शर्मीला लड़का · शर्मीली लड़की · शर्मीले लोग.
- Most others never change: **मेहनती, आलसी, बातूनी, शांत** — and **मज़ाकिया**, even though it ends in -आ.
- **दिल का अच्छा** 'good-hearted'; for a woman **दिल की अच्छी**. Same with स्वभाव: शांत स्वभाव **का / की**.
- 'What's he like?' = **वो कैसा इंसान है?**

lessons.title: The good and the not-so-good

tip.title: Softening: थोड़ा and -सा
tip.body:
- Hindi softens criticism with **थोड़ा** 'a bit' and **-सा** '-ish': वो **थोड़ा** घमंडी है · वो **अजीब-सा** है.
- Both agree like -आ adjectives: थोड़ी अजीब-**सी** लड़की, थोड़े अजीब-**से** लोग.
- 'Not at all': **ज़रा भी नहीं** / **बिल्कुल नहीं**.

lessons.title: Looks and first impressions

tip.title: लगना and दिखना — seems, looks
tip.body:
- **लगना** = seem: वो थका हुआ **लग रहा है**, वो अच्छी **लगती है** 'she seems nice'.
- Trap: **मुझे** वो अच्छी लगती है = **I like her**!
- **दिखना**, **दिखने में** = looks, appearance: दिखने में स्मार्ट है.
- Looks like someone: माँ **जैसी** दिखती है (जैसा agrees).
- **लगता है…** = 'it looks like…'.
tip.pattern: वो + adjective + लगता / दिखता है · X जैसा

sentences.native: वो थका हुआ लग रहा है, सब ठीक है?
sentences.roman: vo thakā huā lag rahā hai, sab ṭhīk hai?
sentences.en: He looks tired, is everything OK?

sentences.native: दिखने में वो बिल्कुल अपने पापा जैसा है।
sentences.roman: dikhne meṃ vo bilkul apne pāpā jaisā hai.
sentences.en: He's the spitting image of his dad.

sentences.native: वो कद में छोटी है, चश्मा पहनती है और बाल लंबे हैं।
sentences.roman: vo kad meṃ chhoṭī hai, chashmā pahantī hai aur bāl lambe haiṃ.
sentences.en: She's short, wears glasses and has long hair.

sentences.native: मुझे वो लड़का अच्छा लगता है।
sentences.roman: mujhe vo laṛkā achchhā lagtā hai.
sentences.en: I like that boy.

sentences.native: सच बताओ, तुम्हें वो अच्छी लगती है ना?
sentences.roman: sach batāo, tumheṃ vo achchhī lagtī hai nā?
sentences.en: Be honest, you like her, don't you?

sentences.native: वो पहली बार में घमंडी लगती है, पर है नहीं।
sentences.roman: vo pahlī bār meṃ ghamaṇḍī lagtī hai, par hai nahīṃ.
sentences.en: She seems stuck-up at first, but she isn't.

sentences.native: चश्मे में तुम बिल्कुल अपने दादा जी जैसे लगते हो!
sentences.roman: chashme meṃ tum bilkul apne dādā jī jaise lagte ho!
sentences.en: In those glasses you look just like your grandad!

sentences.native: वो कैसा दिखता है? लंबा है?
sentences.roman: vo kaisā dikhtā hai? lambā hai?
sentences.en: What does he look like? Is he tall?

sentences.native: लगता है वो आज बहुत ग़ुस्से में है।
sentences.roman: lagtā hai vo āj bahut ġusse meṃ hai.
sentences.en: Looks like he's really angry today.

lessons.title: Pointing people out: the one who…

tip.title: जो, जिसका, जिसने — the one who…
tip.body:
- Pair **जो** … **वो**: **जो** लड़की लाल कुर्ते में है, **वो** मेरी बहन है.
- जो changes like वो: **जिस** + postposition (जिससे, जिसके साथ), **जिसका** 'whose', **जिसने** (with ने), **जिसे** 'whom'. Plural: **जिन**, जिनका, जिन्होंने.
- Shortcut: **वाला**: चश्मे **वाला** लड़का 'the guy with glasses'.

sentences.native: जो लड़की लाल कुर्ते में है, वो मेरी बहन है।
sentences.roman: jo laṛkī lāl kurte meṃ hai, vo merī bahan hai.
sentences.en: The girl in the red kurta is my sister.

sentences.native: जिस लड़के से मैं कल मिली थी, वो बहुत मज़ाकिया था।
sentences.roman: jis laṛke se maiṃ kal milī thī, vo bahut mazākiyā thā.
sentences.en: The guy I met yesterday was really funny. (woman speaking)

sentences.native: जिसका बर्थडे है, वो कहाँ है?
sentences.roman: jiskā barthḍe hai, vo kahāṃ hai?
sentences.en: Where's the birthday boy?

sentences.native: जिसने यह कहा, वो झूठ बोल रहा है।
sentences.roman: jisne yah kahā, vo jhūṭh bol rahā hai.
sentences.en: Whoever said that is lying.

sentences.native: वो दोस्त, जिसके साथ मैं रहता हूँ, बहुत आलसी है।
sentences.roman: vo dost, jiske sāth maiṃ rahtā hūṃ, bahut ālsī hai.
sentences.en: The friend I live with is really lazy. (man speaking)

sentences.native: हम बचपन के दोस्त हैं, हमारी दोस्ती बहुत पुरानी है।
sentences.roman: ham bachpan ke dost haiṃ, hamārī dostī bahut purānī hai.
sentences.en: We're childhood friends, we go back a long way.

sentences.native: जिन रिश्तेदारों को मैं जानता भी नहीं, वो भी शादी में आए।
sentences.roman: jin rishtedāroṃ ko maiṃ jāntā bhī nahīṃ, vo bhī shādī meṃ āye.
sentences.en: Even relatives I don't know came to the wedding.

sentences.native: वो चश्मे वाली लड़की कौन है?
sentences.roman: vo chashme vālī laṛkī kaun hai?
sentences.en: Who's that girl with the glasses?

sentences.native: मेरा एक रिश्तेदार है जो पुलिस में है।
sentences.roman: merā ek rishtedār hai jo pulis meṃ hai.
sentences.en: I've got a relative who's in the police.

sentences.native: जहाँ हम पहली बार मिले थे, वो कैफ़े अब बंद हो गया।
sentences.roman: jahāṃ ham pahlī bār mile the, vo kaife ab band ho gayā.
sentences.en: The café where we first met has closed down now.

lessons.title: Partners and in-laws

tip.title: A word for every relative
tip.body:
- **भाभी** brother's wife · **जीजा जी** sister's husband · **सास** mother-in-law.
- Use them instead of names: 'भाभी, चाय?' — never the first name of an older in-law.
- Modern relationships are in English: **बॉयफ़्रेंड, गर्लफ़्रेंड, डेट करना, सिंगल**.
- Getting on: **X की Y से (नहीं) बनती** 'X does(n't) get on with Y'.

new: वो किसी को डेट कर रहा है?

sentences.native: उसका बॉयफ़्रेंड बहुत समझदार है।
sentences.roman: uskā boyfrenḍ bahut samajhdār hai.
sentences.en: Her boyfriend's really understanding.

sentences.native: तुम्हारी गर्लफ़्रेंड कहाँ की है?
sentences.roman: tumhārī garlfrenḍ kahāṃ kī hai?
sentences.en: Where's your girlfriend from?

sentences.native: मेरी भाभी और मम्मी की आपस में बहुत अच्छी बनती है।
sentences.roman: merī bhābhī aur mammī kī āpas meṃ bahut achchhī bantī hai.
sentences.en: My sister-in-law and my mum get on really well.

sentences.native: जीजा जी बहुत मज़ाकिया हैं।
sentences.roman: jījā jī bahut mazākiyā haiṃ.
sentences.en: My brother-in-law is really funny.

sentences.native: दीदी की सगाई अगले महीने है।
sentences.roman: dīdī kī sagāī agle mahīne hai.
sentences.en: My sister's engagement is next month.

sentences.native: घरवाले उसके लिए रिश्ता ढूँढ रहे हैं।
sentences.roman: gharvāle uske liye rishtā ḍhūṃḍh rahe haiṃ.
sentences.en: His family are looking for a match for him.

sentences.native: नहीं, वो किसी को डेट नहीं कर रहा, अभी सिंगल है।
sentences.roman: nahīṃ, vo kisī ko ḍeṭ nahīṃ kar rahā, abhī siṅgal hai.
sentences.en: No, he's not seeing anyone, he's single at the moment.

sentences.native: उसकी सास बहुत अच्छी हैं, बिल्कुल माँ जैसी।
sentences.roman: uskī sās bahut achchhī haiṃ, bilkul māṃ jaisī.
sentences.en: Her mother-in-law is lovely, just like a mother.

sentences.native: उनका रिश्ता दो साल पुराना है।
sentences.roman: unkā rishtā do sāl purānā hai.
sentences.en: They've been together for two years.

sentences.native: भाई और जीजा जी की आपस में नहीं बनती।
sentences.roman: bhāī aur jījā jī kī āpas meṃ nahīṃ bantī.
sentences.en: My brother and my brother-in-law don't get on.

tip.title: Passing on what you've heard
tip.body:
- **सुना है (कि)…** 'I've heard / apparently': सुना है उनकी सगाई हो गई.
- **लोग कहते हैं** 'people say' · **लगता है** 'it looks like'.
- Swearing someone to secrecy: **किसी को बताना मत!**
- Getting out of it: **छोड़ो, हमें क्या!** 'none of our business!'

sentences.native: सुना है, उनका कल बहुत बड़ा झगड़ा हुआ।
sentences.roman: sunā hai, unkā kal bahut baṛā jhagṛā huā.
sentences.en: Apparently they had a massive row yesterday.

sentences.native: सुना है कि प्रिया की सगाई हो गई!
sentences.roman: sunā hai ki Priyā kī sagāī ho gaī!
sentences.en: I've heard Priya's got engaged!

sentences.native: सच है या बस अफ़वाह है?
sentences.roman: sach hai yā bas afvāh hai?
sentences.en: Is it true or just a rumour?

sentences.native: लोग कहते हैं कि वो बहुत घमंडी है, पर मुझे ऐसा नहीं लगता।
sentences.roman: log kahte haiṃ ki vo bahut ghamaṇḍī hai, par mujhe aisā nahīṃ lagtā.
sentences.en: People say she's really stuck-up, but I don't think so.

sentences.native: यार, पीठ पीछे चुग़ली मत करो।
sentences.roman: yār, pīṭh pīchhe chuġlī mat karo.
sentences.en: Come on, don't talk about people behind their backs.

sentences.native: मैं तुम्हें एक बात बताऊँ? पर किसी को बताना मत!
sentences.roman: maiṃ tumheṃ ek bāt batāūṃ? par kisī ko batānā mat!
sentences.en: Shall I tell you something? But don't tell anyone!

sentences.native: लगता है उन दोनों में कुछ चल रहा है।
sentences.roman: lagtā hai un donoṃ meṃ kuchh chal rahā hai.
sentences.en: Looks like something's going on between those two.

sentences.native: छोड़ो, हमें क्या! उनकी ज़िंदगी है।
sentences.roman: chhoṛo, hameṃ kyā! unkī zindagī hai.
sentences.en: Forget it, it's none of our business! It's their life.

sentences.native: यह बात तुम्हें किसने बताई?
sentences.roman: yah bāt tumheṃ kisne batāī?
sentences.en: Who told you that?

sentences.native: वो सबकी चुग़ली करती है, उस पर भरोसा मत करना।
sentences.roman: vo sabkī chuġlī kartī hai, us par bharosā mat karnā.
sentences.en: She gossips about everyone, don't trust her.
